column1: # Shiren GB — THE GLOSSARY. 391 item, monster, appearance and NPC names.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS FROZEN
# `こんぼう` is an item name, a line of help text, a combat message and a shop's dialogue.
# Translated batch by batch it becomes Club / Cudgel / Stick, and review cannot catch that
# -- catching it means holding 1,263 strings in your head at once. So the names are
# translated ONCE, here, and every later batch takes them as a constraint.
# `tools/lint_en.py --glossary` enforces it: if a Japanese string contains a glossary
# term, the English must use the frozen rendering.
#   * Names read as modern official Shiren English -- plain and meaning-first -- rather
#     than as the Aeon Genesis SNES romanisations. `ひとつめゴロシ` is "One-Eye Killer",
#   * The CATEGORY nouns are Aeon Genesis', so the two projects agree where it is cheapest
#     for them to: Herb / Bracer / Staff / Pot / Scroll. (`~/Documents/Workplace/Shiren/
#   * A tier family reads as a family: Rat Minion / Rat Boss / Rat Kingpin.
#   * Proper nouns that carry no meaning in Japanese either stay transliterated --
# THE CAPS ARE A DECREE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. See HANDOFF_NEXT.md §4.
# A combat line and the name substituted into it share the same 24-cell line, so widening
# a cap to fit a name quietly shortens every combat line in the game. If a name does not
# fit, REWORD THE NAME. `lint_en.py --glossary` fails the build on an over-cap name.
# THE ITEM LIST AGREES, and this one IS measured (2026-08-04, `build/glossary_widest.png`).
# The inventory box is 18 tiles wide and byte 0 is the cursor, so it holds 17 cells. A
# 16-cell name renders complete and uncut, with one cell to spare:
# So 16 is the ceiling on both paths at once, and the decree and the box happen to agree.
# Do not read that as slack -- 17 would fit the list and still truncate a combat line.
# DUPLICATE JAPANESE IS NORMAL AND MUST STAY DUPLICATE. `くねくねハニー`, `オロチ`,
# `いやしウサギ`, `ばくだんウニ`, `ぼうれいむしゃ` and `エーテルもどき` each appear at
# two or three tiers with the same name in Japanese; they keep one English name. What the
# collision check forbids is the reverse -- two DIFFERENT Japanese names landing on the
# same English, which would make two monsters indistinguishable in a message.
# `New Weapon 3` and friends are unused placeholder slots (`しんきぶき3` = 新規武器3).
# They are named rather than left Japanese so that a slot leaking on screen is legible.
